name: HONEYWELL INTERNATIONAL INC.
naics_description: OTHER AIRCRAFT PARTS AND AUXILIARY EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged Honeywell International for statistical anomalies. Benford's Law analysis of leading digits in award amounts shows significant deviation from expected frequency, with digit 1 appearing 19.5% of the time versus the expected 30.1%, and digit 5 appearing 9.5% versus expected 7.9%. A parent contract modification grew at a rate 4,427 times its initial value, vastly outpacing the 62-fold average growth ratio for peers in aircraft parts manufacturing. The entity also scores as a multivariate outlier, driven partly by concentration of all 2,082 awards from a single agency. Additionally, sole-source awards comprise 92.2% of its portfolio, substantially above the 45.5% median for comparable manufacturers.

The modification detector registered a z-score of 5.35 sigmas, indicating very unusual growth concentration. Benford's test yielded a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.111 with p-value 1.45e-22 across 2,082 transactions. The isolation forest anomaly score was 0.785 on a 0-to-1 scale. Sole-source concentration z-score was 1.21 sigmas, with 1,920 of 2,082 awards awarded without competition.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not prove misconduct. Honeywell is a major defense contractor with legitimate reasons for high sole-source work on specialized aircraft components and long-term production contracts subject to frequent modifications. The single-agency concentration reflects its primary DoD relationship. The Benford deviation may reflect genuine clustering of contract values around standard price points in aerospace manufacturing rather than manipulation. The peer group for this NAICS includes 322 firms of vastly different scales, potentially limiting comparability.
